title: Money as a PHP float loses precision (0.1+0.2 != 0.3); plus a loose == "0" comparison on the total
sourceContent:
<?php
// invoice.php - line total with float money (precision trap)
function lineTotal($price, $qty) {
    // TRAP: PHP floats can't represent decimal money exactly
    // (0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3). Money must be a decimal type in the target.
    $total = $price * $qty;
    // TRAP: loose comparison of a float to an int-looking string.
    if ($total == "0") {
        return 0.0;
    }
    return round($total, 2);
}
notes: Money computed and stored as a PHP float can't represent decimals exactly, so the target must use BigDecimal/decimal, never double. There is also a loose $total == "0" comparison (float vs numeric string) that must become an explicit typed check. The invariant is total = price*qty rounded to 2dp.
